summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: Making a Knotted Triangle Scarf (Part 2) - Making the Knot ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will guide you through the process of creating a knotted triangle scarf using Marvelous Designer. We will focus on making the knot and ensuring that all components are properly aligned and sewn together. ## Setting Up the Cut-Off Line The length of the cut-off line can be used to draw a rectangle as a cut-off. If you are not sure, you can directly use a **30mm wide** and **150mm high** measurement. ## Positioning the Board Use the positioning ball to drag the board to the back of the virtual model. - Reduce the diameter of the particle to **3** so that the smaller board can adequately cover the cut-off position of the large board. - Reduce the thickness of the collision to **1**. If you are unsure about the size of the small partner, use the positioning tool located on the upper right of the positioning ball to locate the board near the collision position. ## Opening and Folding the Board After confirming the position, open the board in the horizontal direction. - Create an inner line along the opening position and fold it. - Open the texture surface, check the back of the board, and then use the fold arrangement tool to fold the board to ensure that the front is facing out. ## Pinning and Sewing On the four corners of this board, add four pins to make it convenient to rotate the board. - Sew the boards on both sides to form a pipe. - Open the model. When pressing **Shift**, click on the pin to select more pins. When opening the model, select the bottom two pins and move them with the positioning tool. If you want to rotate, rotate the pin with the last click as the center. Rotate **360 degrees**, which is equivalent to rotating a circle in the middle of this pipe. ## Closing and Hardening the Pipe Close the two ends of the pipe and harden the board; otherwise, the material will be too soft, making it inconvenient for the scarf to pass through. Then, sew the two ends of the pipe together. Press **W** to click on the pin to delete the existing pin. Delete the two pins on the first end. Open the model; this end will automatically be sewn to a fixed position, and the whole board will be fixed in **3D space**. It won't fall. When it's stable, stop the simulation and move the whole board to the position of the scarf. ## Adjusting the Board Length After comparison, it can be seen that the whole board is now very difficult to pass through directly. However, we can use more than **100 soles**. For now, the length of this board has reached the purpose of passing through the scarf. If you are not sure of the end-to-end, use the editing tool. The board needs to grow along the vertical direction, so the length of the arrowhead is increased. That is, the slope of the gold. Open the simulation first and change the slope. Then pause the simulation and place the board near the scarf board. Open the simulation again to let the circle interact with the frozen board first. ## Continuing the Simulation Unscrew all the scarf boards. Since the headboard is now stable, simulate it. Delete the fixed pin on the headboard. Unscrew the hardening and continue to simulate. Automatically move the headboard to the next position. We need to copy two such boards and combine them. After selecting the fixed pin, in the menu on the right-hand tab, you can also choose to delete. Delete the fixed pin in the two headboards. After simulation again, copy and paste the board in the **3D window**. After copying a board, adjust its arrangement position to avoid interference with the scarf. Simulate it and then copy and paste another board. Due to the fact that each circle has been rotated by itself so far, the effect of keeping these intersections will be more realistic after the merger. ## Final Adjustments After wearing it, reduce the slope to **120**. After simulation, drag the board so that the scarf is in a position that can be seen. Do not let it be squeezed inside, as this will affect the merger later. In the position of the three boards separated in the **2D window**, ensure there are no overlapping parts. Then delete the line used to close the line between the boards. Re-create the cross sewing line. ## Simulation and Review After the intersection is created, you can simulate it and observe the effect. If you tighten the force for a moment, the board will be separated. Create a dipping line in the same way as in the video. Now this is fine because it will tighten and loosen after a while, and it will not disperse after tightening. Once the molding is stable, gradually return the loosen rate from **120** to **100**. Do not tighten it all at once, as the cut-off plate may become unstable if the grid suddenly becomes smaller. ## Merging and Finalizing In the simulation process, if there is more space for the fabric, drag the plate to cover each other. Reduce the loosen rate to **90** again to tighten the cut-off more. You can see that as the loosen rate decreases, the gap in the middle becomes more pronounced. Eliminate the straight line left because of the spread to facilitate the continuation of the merge later. Use the editor sewing line tool, select the sewing line, and choose merge in the right-click menu. You can merge along the sewing line to create a whole cut-off plate. If there is no stability in the simulation, you can continue to open the simulation, pause it, and perform short simulations. ## Conclusion After the cut-off or merge operation of the plate, the sewing needle will automatically be deleted. Please re-create it. If the pull of the sewing needle is more severe, you can manually adjust the position with the editor sewing needle. You will notice that the cut-off pattern becomes less visible. Thank you for watching this tutorial. I hope you found it helpful. If you enjoyed this video, please subscribe for more content. See you in the next video! ```
